comparison: Perfect agreement on BASH MaP methodology (C12-C18). Both evaluations find the method well-supported with strong experimental evidence. OpenEval emphasizes specific technical details (conversion efficiency, misincorporation signatures), while peer reviewers confirm the method's validity and ability to detect N7-methyl-G adducts sensitive to structural context.

Complete agreement on technical validation (C19-C21). Both evaluations support the high correlation, Watson-Crick face preservation, and ROC analysis. Peer reviewers implicitly affirm these claims by noting that BASH MaP retains DMS MaP information while adding new guanosine data.

Strong agreement on G-quadruplex identification capability (C22-C24). Both evaluations affirm the method's ability to distinguish G-quadruplex structures. OpenEval includes C25-C26 (polyUG data) which peer reviewers address separately in R4. Both note differential reactivity patterns as key evidence.

Agreement on N7G vs N1G comparison (C27-C28) and polyUG validation (C25-C26 from peer R4). OpenEval focuses on the superiority of N7G reactivity, while peer reviewers accept the overall structural context sensitivity including polyUG data without specific concerns.

Agreement on in-cell application (C29, C35-C36, C68-C69, C77). Both evaluations support the cellular data, though with different emphases. OpenEval notes the unusual topology prediction would benefit from additional validation, while peer reviewers view this as 'encouraging preliminary results' representing a potential major advance for the field.

Complete agreement on single-molecule analysis advantages (C30-C33, C73). Both evaluations affirm the G-G correlation patterns and network clustering capabilities. Peer reviewers explicitly note the increased misincorporations per transcript make BASH MaP more amenable to co-occurring misincorporation analysis.

Agreement on M2 BASH MaP mutate-and-map results (C37-C40, C80-C82). Both evaluations support the global destabilization findings and base-stacking interpretations. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the 'wide range of useful probing analyses' without raising specific concerns.

Significant disagreement on DAGGER computational approach (C41-C42, C83-C93). OpenEval finds strong validation and clear improvement over existing methods. However, peer reviewers raise substantial concerns about robustness and generalizability, noting three key limitations: single-read folding doesn't represent single-molecule folding, G residues in loops vs G-quadruplexes have different impacts, and the method requires prior 3D structure knowledge.

Agreement on conformational heterogeneity resolution (C43-C49, C97-C98, C101). Both evaluations support the DANCE deconvolution results and ability to identify two Spinach states. OpenEval includes C97 (DMS MaP failure comparison) and emphasizes reasonable agreement with fluorescence measurements, while peer reviewers focus on the broad analytical capabilities.

Agreement on functional validation of misfolding mechanism (C50-C51, C104-C105). Both evaluations accept the fluorescence assay results supporting loop A interactions with G-quadruplex G's. Peer reviewers do not challenge these mutagenesis results, accepting them as validation of the BASH MaP-derived structural model.

Agreement on misfolding mechanism evidence (C52-C54, C106-C108). Both evaluations support the computational clustering and Spinach-Broccoli structural comparisons. Peer reviewers note that BASH MaP-derived data helps with secondary structure prediction for Spinach RNA.

Complete agreement on overall conclusions (C55, C113-C114). Both evaluations affirm that BASH MaP represents a significant methodological advance. The editor explicitly states this work 'substantially advances our understanding of RNA structure analysis,' and all reviewers confirm the method provides valuable structural information.

Agreement on scientific rationale and background (C1-C7, C56-C60, C109-C112). Both evaluations support these claims as established facts and prior knowledge. OpenEval emphasizes the logical necessity for detecting N7G modifications, while peer reviewers accept these as uncontroversial context for the new method.

Agreement on G-quadruplex biology background (C8-C11). Both evaluations accept these as accurate background supported by appropriate citations. These establish biological importance without being novel findings of the study.

Agreement on structural features validation (C61-C63). OpenEval notes these validate the method's ability to detect known structural features, while peer reviewers accept them as established facts providing context. Both view these observations as consistent with prior knowledge.

Agreement on polyUG conformations and N1G/N7G comparison (C64-C66). OpenEval provides specific figure references for register analysis and reactivity comparisons, while peer reviewers accept these as supporting observations without challenge.

Agreement on methodological background (C67, C70-C71, C78-C79, C94-C96, C100, C102-C103). Both evaluations support these claims as established prior work with appropriate citations. These provide rationale for method development and analysis approaches.

OpenEval evaluates network analysis observations and mechanistic interpretations (C34, C74-C76) as supported, noting the global destabilization hypothesis is reasonable but acknowledged as unclear in mechanism. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval rates C99 as UNCERTAIN, noting it is explicitly speculative without direct experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific speculative claim about measurement discrepancies.
